labels.text: How can I help you today?

S7.01.note: The exact control that starts a new chat was not confirmed in the code; the empty-state layout is in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx.
steps: Sign in and open a new, empty chat.
Look at the centre of the window: the greeting and the message box should sit in the middle.
Confirm there is no empty transcript area above the message box.
S7.01.where: Open a new chat (first screen after sign-in) > centre of the window shows the greeting 'Good morning' (or afternoon/evening) and the message box

steps: Ask a question that gets a long text answer.
Make the window wide.
Check that the answer text stays in a centred column of readable width instead of running across the full window.
S7.02.where: Any chat with a long answer; the reading column is a layout rule with no control

S7.03.needs: a chat answer that contains a table
S7.03.note: Full-width behaviour of the expanded view was located by the button code, not run.
steps: Ask for an answer that contains a wide table (for example a comparison table).
Hover over the table and click 'Expand table'.
Check that the expanded table uses the full window width and closes with 'Close expanded table'.
S7.03.where: A table in a chat answer > hover the table > 'Expand table' button

S7.04.needs: a chat that has created an artifact
steps: Ask for a document or code file so that an artifact is created.
Click the 'Artifacts' button or the artifact card.
Check that the artifact opens in a pane beside the conversation and that you can scroll and type in both.
S7.04.where: Chat with an artifact > 'Artifacts' button (title 'Artifacts') to open the artifacts panel beside the conversation

S7.05.note: The control that opens the research panel from an answer was not traced.
steps: Run a research question that produces cited sources.
Open the research panel beside the conversation.
Select the 'Sources' tab and check that sources are listed beside the transcript, which stays visible.
S7.05.where: Research panel > tab group 'Research views' > 'Sources' tab

S7.07.needs: a coding session that has changes or a terminal
S7.07.note: The changes button label was not found as text; it has no visible word in the grep.
steps: Open a coding session from the 'Code' view.
Open the changes view (button next to the terminal icon in the session header).
Check that the conversation and the code workspace (changes, diffs, terminal) are visible together.
S7.07.where: Top toggle 'Code' (the code surface) > open a coding session > chat with the code workspace (changes, terminal)

S7.08.note: The default layout is 'tiled', so the button shows 'Stack panes' first. How a second session is added to the panes was not traced.
steps: Open two or more coding sessions.
Check that they appear side by side in the pane area.
Click the layout button and check that each session remains usable (type, scroll) in its own pane.
S7.08.where: Code > a coding session with two or more live sessions open > 'Stack panes' or 'Place panes side by side' button in the pane header

S7.09.note: The button reads 'Place panes side by side' once the layout is stacked.
steps: Open two or more coding sessions so that the panes appear.
Click 'Stack panes'.
Check that the sessions are one above the other and each can still be used.
S7.09.where: Code > two or more live sessions open > 'Stack panes' button in the pane header

S7.11.needs: an artifact to open the panel
S7.11.note: The research and work panels use the same handle with 'Resize research panel' and 'Resize <panel name>'.
steps: Open the artifacts panel beside a conversation.
Drag the left edge of the panel, or click the edge and press the Left or Right arrow key.
Check that the panel width changes and the conversation reflows.
S7.11.where: Chat > 'Artifacts' panel open > drag the left edge (separator 'Resize artifacts panel')

steps: Sign in and look at the left sidebar.
Click the 'Collapse sidebar' button, or press Command+B.
Check that the sidebar folds away; click 'Expand sidebar' to bring it back and confirm it reopens.
S7.12.where: Sidebar toggle button 'Collapse sidebar' (it reads 'Expand sidebar' when closed); keyboard Command+B on Mac or Ctrl+B elsewhere

labels.text: Move ${panelLabel} back to the main window

S7.14.needs: the desktop app and a research or task panel
S7.14.note: Labels are template strings; the panel name fills in at run time.
steps: In the desktop app, open a research answer or a task panel.
Click the button 'Open <panel name> in a new window' in the panel header.
Check that the panel opens in its own window and can be used there; then click 'Move <panel name> back to the main window' to return it.
S7.14.where: Research panel or Details (work) panel header > button 'Open <panel name> in a new window'; to return, 'Move <panel name> back to the main window'

S7.15.note: The expanded box is taller (about 60 percent of the screen height), not a true full-screen editor.
steps: Type a long prompt into the message box.
Click the 'Expand message input' button in the top-right corner of the box.
Check that the box becomes taller for editing, then press Escape or click the button again to return to the chat.
S7.15.where: Message box > 'Expand message input' button at its top-right corner; Escape returns it to normal size

steps: Open a research report from a deep research answer.
Click 'Read report full screen'.
Read the report in the full-screen view, then click 'Exit full screen' to return to the chat.
S7.16.where: Research report > 'Read report full screen' button (title 'Full screen'); 'Exit full screen' returns

S7.17.needs: a chat with an image attachment or image in a reply
S7.17.note: Video viewing was not confirmed; the viewer code covers images.
steps: Send or open a message that contains an image.
Click the image to open it.
Use 'Zoom in' or 'Zoom out', then click 'Close preview' and check that you are back at the chat.
S7.17.where: Chat > an image in a message > click it to open the 'Image preview' viewer; 'Close preview' dismisses it

S7.18.note: The always-on-top behaviour was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Click 'Quick Ask' in the menu bar, or press the Quick Ask shortcut.
Switch to another app and check the small Quick Ask window stays on top of it.
Press the shortcut again to hide it.
S7.18.where: Desktop app menu bar > 'Quick Ask' (or the Quick Ask shortcut)

S7.19.note: The panel is set to 480 by 620 pixels; the missing sidebar was not confirmed in the page code.
steps: Click 'Quick Ask' in the menu bar.
Check that the small panel opens without the full sidebar or side panels.
Ask a quick question and check the answer fits the small window.
S7.19.where: Desktop app menu bar > 'Quick Ask' opens the small companion panel (route /quick-ask)

steps: Open a chat with many messages.
Scroll the transcript up and down.
Check that the message box stays at the bottom of the window while the messages scroll above it.
S7.20.where: Any chat with a long conversation; the composer is a layout rule with no control

S7.21.note: The growth happens in the code, and the button appears only when the text is long enough.
steps: Click the message box and type or paste a long prompt that wraps onto several lines.
Check that the box grows taller as you type.
Click 'Expand message input' to make it larger, then click it again to shrink it.
S7.21.where: Message box > type a long prompt > 'Expand message input' button appears at the top-right corner

S7.22.needs: a long conversation; optionally an open side panel
S7.22.note: The 'Scroll to bottom' button appears when the transcript is scrolled up; it is not part of the layout rule itself.
steps: Open a long chat and scroll the transcript.
Check that the side panel, the header and the message box do not move.
Scroll a side panel (if open) and check that the transcript does not move.
S7.22.where: Any long chat; the independent scroll is a layout rule with no control

S7.23.note: No sticky class was found in the artifacts folder, so the toolbar pinning was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Open a long artifact in the artifacts panel.
Scroll the artifact content down.
Check that the toolbar buttons ('Preview', 'Source', 'Version history') stay visible at the top.
S7.23.where: Artifact panel with a long artifact open; the sticky toolbar is a layout rule, its buttons are 'Preview' and 'Source'

S7.24.needs: a long table in a chat answer
steps: Ask for an answer with a long table (many rows).
Scroll the table or the transcript so the top of the table leaves the screen.
Check that the table header row stays pinned at the top while the rows scroll.
S7.24.where: A long table in a chat answer; the pinned header is a style rule with no control

S7.25.needs: phone width or a narrow window
S7.25.note: Overlay mode is set by the layout value in the code; the exact width threshold was not read.
steps: Open the artifacts panel beside a conversation.
Make the window narrow.
Check that the panel moves over the conversation as an overlay and returns beside it when the window is wide again.
S7.25.where: Narrow the window with the artifacts panel open; the panel turns into an overlay labelled 'Artifacts'

S7.29.note: Limits are MIN_SIDE_PANEL_WIDTH and MAX_SIDE_PANEL_WIDTH; the desktop window minimum is set in apps/desktop/electron/main.ts.
steps: Open the artifacts panel.
Drag the 'Resize artifacts panel' handle as far left as it goes, then as far right as it goes.
Check that the panel stops at a minimum and a maximum width and the conversation keeps a usable width.
S7.29.where: Drag any resize handle ('Resize artifacts panel') to its far limits; the minimum and maximum widths are enforced in code

steps: Click 'Collapse sidebar' and resize the artifacts panel.
Close the app or reload the page, then open it again.
Check that the sidebar is still collapsed and the panel is still the width you set.
S7.30.where: Collapse the sidebar or resize a panel, then reopen the app; the saved choice is restored

S7.31.needs: the desktop app; a second monitor for the monitor part
steps: In the desktop app, resize and move the window.
Quit the app and open it again.
Check that the window opens at the same size and position; with a second monitor, unplug it and check the window is still on screen.
S7.31.where: Desktop app window; resize and move the window, then quit and reopen it

S7.32.needs: a conversation that has messages; a printer or Save as PDF in the print dialog
S7.32.note: The plan file's "Where to find it" line says not written yet, which is stale: the Print item exists in ConversationTitleMenu.tsx and the print CSS is in apps/web/app/globals.css (@media print, line 1862). "Conversation options" is an aria-label, not visible text. The print flow is in apps/web/features/chat/lib/print-conversation.ts. The Electron desktop shows the same web page, and no native desktop Print menu item was found. No print path for reports was found, only conversations.
steps: Sign in and open a conversation that already has messages.
Click the Conversation options button in the top header of the chat. It is an icon button with no visible text, so look for the button labelled Conversation options.
Click Print in the menu.
The system print dialog opens. In the preview, check that the sidebar, top bar, toolbar and message box are gone, and that the whole conversation is shown.
Check that the page is white with dark text, and that long messages break across pages without splitting a sentence mid-line.
S7.32.where: Open a conversation that has messages > Conversation options (icon button in the chat header) > Print
